messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT — service: inference-serving-us-west — trigger: p95 latency spike on /v1/generate. Current p95 ~1.8s (baseline 0.28s). Error rate 3.4% and rising. Affected cluster: inference-pool-usw-2. PagerDuty: paged primary oncall (maya). Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1736001234

maya: I'm primary for the shift, saw the alert. I'm on the primary console now. Heads up I'm scheduled to hand off in ~12m for timezone swap — I'll stay until it's stable or until we do a warm handoff.

sam: I'm the secondary, currently in transit but online on mobile. ETA for being fully available ~10m. If handoff happens before I'm at a keyboard, lia can take over.

lia: noted. I'll be available in ~25m (just finishing another sync). If you need a hard handoff, leave clear state: impact, mitigations, next steps, and which runbook step you're on.

maya: quick triage notes:
- observed spike right after a scheduled batch job at 12:10 UTC.
- restarted inference pool pods on usw-2, no immediate fix.
- sampling logs: several 504s and increased queue times.

Commands I ran:
```
# restart pool pods in us-west cluster
kubectl -n serving-usw2 rollout restart deploy/inference-pool-usw2
# check tail logs for errors
kubectl -n serving-usw2 logs deploy/inference-pool-usw2 --since=15m | grep -i "timeout\|504" | tail -n 50
# query recent error rate
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?service=inference&window=5m&metric=error_rate' | jq .
```

Log snippet: "2026-03-14T12:12:03Z inference-pool requestId=abc123 status=504 queued_ms=1200 backend_ms=580"

maya: immediate mitigation applied: enabled temporary traffic-shed to shift ~30% of requests to standby pool (serving-usw-standby) to cut load. Command:
```
redwood-routing set-weight --from inference-pool-usw2 --to inference-pool-usw-standby --percent 30 --reason "latency mitigation"
```

ops-lead: paging/escalation reminder (copying ops runbook):
- 0m: Alert hits primary oncall (maya) — primary acknowledges in PagerDuty.
- 0-5m: Triage and quick mitigations (restarts, traffic-shed, config rollback).
- 5-15m: If latency or error_rate >5% or customer-facing errors continue, page secondary (sam) and infra-sre.
- 15-30m: Escalate to SRE Manager (@ops-lead) and Model Runtime owner. Open incident bridge if not already.
- 30m+: If >20% customer impact or paying tenant SLA hit, page Eng Director and CS leadership.

ops-lead: immediate paging decisions for this thread: please page infra-sre and model-runtime now (they're marked critical for tail-latency issues). Also notify cs_oncall for potential customer comms.

incident-bot: Update: error rate climbed to 7.1% in last 5m. Alert severity auto-bumped. Incident bridge: https://meet.internal/incident/1736001234

maya: infra-sre pinged. Model-runtime pinged. I've set a temporary scale-up of the standby pool by +4 replicas as a stop-gap. Command used: `kubectl -n serving-usw2 scale deploy/inference-pool-usw-standby --replicas=8`

lia: handoff checklist (please copy into the warm-handoff message if we swap):
- current impact: p95=1.8s, error_rate=7.1%, affected cluster inference-pool-usw-2, tenants: tenant-X (high), tenant-Y (moderate)
- mitigations in place: traffic-shed 30% -> standby, restarted primary pool, scaled standby +4
- runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving-latency (start at step 2: traffic-shed & scale)
- commands run (paste above) and logs sampled
- next steps: wait 5-10m for metric stabilization, if no improvement rollback last deployment and open infra investigation
- followup ticket: INC-5023 (created, assign to infra-sre)

sam: if I can't make the warm handoff physically, lia please set PagerDuty status for me to 'acknowledged' and then transfer primary. To do manual transfer: `/pd transfer maya -> lia` (ops-lead please confirm transfer playbook).

ops-lead: confirmed transfer playbook: primary must post final state + time and explicitly say "handoff: primary -> new_primary". Secondary should acknowledge. Then update PagerDuty schedule. If handoff happens while incident open, keep incident bridge open and hand off in-bridge.

cs_oncall: notified. Preparing draft comms for tenant-X. If impact persists past 30m we'll send an interim update.

incident-bot: Monitoring: p95 trending down to 1.2s after traffic-shed and scale. Error rate trending to 2.6%. Will post next automated update in 5m.

maya: OK I'm going to start the warm handoff now. Current state posted above, incident bridge is live, infra folks are on it. If you need me I can still respond for 20m but I will be offline for travel after that.

sam: I confirm I'm set to be primary at the end of this handoff. I'll monitor the bridge and metrics, taking over at 12:50 UTC. lia will be secondary.

lia: acknowledged. I'll keep tracking logs and be ready to escalate.

ops-lead: escalation reminders for whoever is primary (sam after handoff): page timeline and who to page next: infra-sre, model-runtime, SRE-manager, eng-director (if >20% impact), cs-lead (customer-facing). Use the incident checklist in the runbook link above.

maya: handoff complete at 12:50 UTC. Leaving residual error_rate ~2.2%, p95 ~0.9s. Followup ticket INC-5023 assigned to infra-sre. New primary: sam. New secondary: lia.

sam: acknowledged and accepted primary at 12:50 UTC. I'll leave this thread open and follow-on with a short postmortem once incident is done.

incident-bot: Incident update: metrics stabilized. Auto-close candidate in 2h if no regression.

ops-lead: good job team. Reminder: update the runbook with the exact commands used for traffic-shed and scale so next time it's one-click.
